paras: The killing of Hunley Royl was the assassination of an elderly Black man living near Newport, Arkansas, by a party of masked men, reported in early March 1888. The only account found is a single line in a weekly state news column, which gave no date, motive or follow-up.

According to the Osceola Times, Royl was "an aged negro, living near Newport" when he "was assassinated by a party of masked men." The item does not say when or how he was killed, how many men took part, or who they were. Nor does it report any accusation against Royl or any reason the men gave for the attack.
No report of an inquest, an arrest or a trial for the killing appears in the coverage.

The Osceola Times printed the report on March 3, 1888, as the opening item of its "Arkansas State News" column on page 2. The single sentence, worded "assassinated" rather than "lynched," carried no headline or comment of its own. It ran beside short items on a death in Texarkana, immigration bureaus and fines remitted by the governor, and next to a longer note on three Ashley County men lodged in the penitentiary "to save them from mob violence."
No other newspaper report of the killing appears in the coverage.

bases: A1 reports an aged Black man killed ('assassinated') by 'a party of masked men', a disguised group killing outside any legal process.

A1 reports a killing by a masked party with no lawful authority, the form of a night-band lynching, but it gives neither the number of men nor any accusation or motive, so group size and pretext are not stated.
The only report found is the one-line roundup item in A1; no other paper, local account, inquest or follow-up was found.
